findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name (or add) a behavioral test that asserts per-request RE-READ semantics — a config/secret value changing between two requests in one MCP session is observed on the second request — so the 'no startup freeze / per-request preserved' claim has an actual oracle.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'Per-request resolution semantics are preserved (no startup freeze)'
Plan asserts the behavioral suites 'are the correctness oracle the AST gate supplements' but does not name a test that observes a mid-session per-request re-read
findings.finding: The plan repeatedly asserts 'per-request resolution semantics are preserved (no startup freeze)' as a core safety property, but relies on the existing 179 unmodified behavioral tests as the oracle without establishing that any of them actually exercise per-request RE-READ semantics (a config/secret value changing between two requests within one server session). If the existing suites only read config once per test, a regression that silently froze config at startup would still pass green.
findings.location: Testing (RED -> GREEN): 'No behavioral delta: the MCP/auth behavioral suites (179 tests) pass UNMODIFIED before and after the cutover.'
scenarios: A resolver in config.py that caches the composed config on first call would freeze config at startup; per-request callers would silently see stale values, yet the unmodified suites (if each reads once) stay green and the cutover closes with a latent behavioral delta.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the specific existing test that varies env/config between two requests in one session, or add an acceptance criterion for one, so the per-request-preservation invariant is proven rather than asserted.
